entries.subject: Source-backed global ultraviolet cloud map to replace the illustrative cloud texture
entries.finding: Akatsuki UVI Level 3b now backs an Ultraviolet lens, so the route the earlier finding called missing exists: tools/objects/akatsuki/uvi-l3b.mts reads the NetCDF-4 grid and the raster lane draws the unobserved side as a declared data gap. What has not been resolved is the subject of this entry. One exposure covers 48.54 per cent of the globe at best, measured over 34 candidates, so the default lens is still the OpenSpace texture, an illustration whose camera, wavelength and colour processing are unresolved. No archive publishes a source-backed global cylindrical UV cloud mosaic: DARTS ships vco_uvi_l3 only as per-exposure 0.125-degree grids, and ESA's VMC mosaic is a northern-hemisphere press strip. Compositing several exposures across one four-day cloud rotation would mix scenes that have moved, which is why this repository has not built it.
entries.revisitWhen: A published global UV cloud mosaic with grid metadata and a permissive licence, or a stated method for compositing Akatsuki L3b exposures that names what it does with cloud motion between them, would let the default cloud lens stop being an illustration.

entries.subject: Akatsuki UVI 365 nm Level 3b exposure as the ultraviolet cloud lens
entries.finding: The Ultraviolet lens is one 365 nm Level 3b exposure, uvi_20230830_100446_365_l3b_v21 from orbit 257, middle 2023-08-30T10:04:46.033 UTC, chosen from 34 candidates by the largest area-weighted lit coverage: 48.54 per cent of the globe at a 3.65-degree phase angle, against a 49.18 per cent visible cap at its 374,422 km range. Orientation was measured rather than assumed: a least-squares fit of the Sun direction to the file's own incidence grid gives a sub-solar point of 206.1913E 2.4897N, and JPL Horizons gives 206.179102E 2.490460N for the same instant in IAU_VENUS with east longitude positive, 0.012 degrees apart in longitude and 0.001 in latitude. The h5wasm decode was checked bitwise identical against h5py for radiance, incidence and both axes. Brightness is the stated transform (radiance x 5e-9) ^ (1/2.2) with white at 2.0e8 W/m2/sr/m, above the exposure's measured maximum 1.8116e8, so nothing clips; there is no photometric normalisation, contrast enhancement or sharpening. The half Akatsuki could not see carries the shared cartographic gap fill.

entries.subject: Photometric law for the lighting overlays
entries.finding: Minnaert coefficients of the cloud tops from MESSENGER MASCS (Pérez-Hoyos et al. 2018, Fig. 2: 1.35 at 657 nm, 1.36 at 547 nm, 1.32 at 467 nm), read from the vector figure because the authors' data file is offline.

entries.subject: Limb halo outside the cloud deck
entries.finding: The halo is a NASA PSG limb profile of PSG's Venus template (VIRA-45 with its sulfuric acid haze), computed on 2026-09-25 with a local nasapsg/psg container: single scattering (NMAX 0, LMAX 41) on 1 km beams at 8 tangent altitudes from the 75 km cloud top to 120 km, the Sun one degree above the tangent point horizon behind the observer, divided by PSG's multiple-scattering disc centre (NMAX 6, LMAX 41, what PSG asks for these aerosols) under an overhead Sun, each band the mean of 5 nm windows. Relative to the disc centre it is 0.039, 0.068 and 0.110 (red, green, blue) at 75 km, 0.016, 0.030 and 0.051 at 80 km and 0.0017, 0.0032 and 0.0057 at 90 km. The first local runs were flat because PUMAS fell back to a two-stream solver for memory and the Sun sat on the horizon; both are now refused by the tool.

entries.subject: A measured limb halo to replace the PSG model
entries.finding: No calibrated limb radiance profile of Venus near full phase in visible bands was found. Pioneer Venus OCPP limb scans at 365 and 690 nm (Lane and Opstbaum 1983) and Venus Express VMC limb images at 513 nm were taken at other phase angles and wavelengths, so they can check the haze height but cannot replace the model.
entries.revisitWhen: A calibrated Venus limb radiance profile in visible bands near full phase is published or archived.

entries.subject: OpenSpace RenderableAtmosphere tuning (Rayleigh and Mie coefficients, flood and sunward shadow releases, terminator ramp)
entries.finding: Removed with atmosphere/model.json; the disc takes the MASCS law.
entries.revisitWhen: Nothing: an authored limb is not reopened once a published law exists.

entries.subject: Magellan global microwave emissivity
entries.finding: The USGS 4641 m signed GeoTIFF is decoded as (DN-1)/10000 with its declared nodata and projection. Antenna and atmosphere corrections are included; emission angle, roughness and tilt are not corrected.

entries.subject: Akatsuki IR2 2.26 micrometre night-side clouds
entries.finding: No full-coverage date sequence was qualified here; this surface emissivity addition retains the existing ultraviolet cloud data.
entries.revisitWhen: A particular Level 3 release and its usable geographic coverage are selected.

entries.subject: Ivanov and Head 2011 geology
entries.finding: The showcase investigation did not establish a reusable numerical GIS product for the published 13-unit map.
entries.revisitWhen: The published GIS units and symbology are acquired with clear reuse terms.

entries.subject: VIRTIS 1 micrometre surface emissivity
entries.finding: A calibrated geographic product and its southern coverage have not been qualified for this release. It is distinct from the Magellan microwave lens.
entries.revisitWhen: The numeric surface-emissivity grid and its atmosphere correction and gaps are established.

entries.subject: Native numeric USGS products and compact display grids
entries.finding: Numeric Magellan GTDR, reflectivity and roughness; emissivity keeps the identity, palette and calibration introduced by #828. Roughness uses the PDS formula because the detached ISIS multiplier conflicts. The evidence records the tested file hashes.

entries.subject: Magellan SAR FMAP left-look global mosaic as the Radar lens
entries.finding: The Radar lens now reads the USGS FMAP left-look mosaic (75 m per pixel from F-BIDRs, cycles 1 and 3; native 506,928 x 230,948 bytes, 83.9996 N to 80.0106 S) through NASA Trek's WMTS zoom 4: 32 x 16 PNG tiles, 8192 x 4096 pixels, 0.0439 degrees (4.64 km) per pixel. The native file is 117 GB and has no overviews, so the Trek pyramid is the bounded route; its reduction kernel is undocumented, but each zoom-4 pixel differs from the mean of its four zoom-5 pixels by 1.2 DN on average against 1.5 to 2.6 DN for any single one, so it averages rather than decimates. Gray is the product DN, 0.2 x DN - 20.2 dB relative to the Muhleman law (USGS product page); the observed median is DN 103 (+0.4 dB), range 15 to 203. Transparent Trek pixels are no-data; partly transparent ones carry the DN averaged with zeros (gray is proportional to alpha), so values are divided by alpha where at least half the footprint is observed (8-bit error at most 1 DN) and marked missing below that. 7.75 per cent of the area between 80 S and 84 N is missing, 8.71 per cent of the globe. Maxwell Montes, Atla Regio and Beta Regio fall where the free-air gravity grid places them, and brightness correlates at r = 0.81 with the C3-MDIR map on the same grid at zero offset. At resolutionScale 4 the lossy-lane atlas (8320 x 6144, q80) is 2,629,358 bytes, 705,862 at scale 2 and 195,760 at scale 1, against 1,012,746 for the previous 2048-wide synthetic-colour atlas; lossless poles 98,866 against 445,994.

entries.subject: USGS C3-MDIR synthetic-colour radar mosaic as its own lens
entries.finding: USGS describes the colourised C3-MDIR mosaic as developed to simulate the surface; its hue is not a measurement. On the 2048 x 1024 WMS image the lens used, colour predicted from brightness alone (the mean RGB of each luma level) leaves an RMS residual of 5.2 DN against a luma spread of 31.2 DN: one black-red-orange-yellow ramp over radar brightness. The lens also added a per-channel exposure curve and sharpening. The FMAP left-look lens shows the same radar brightness at four times the linear detail with a stated decibel scale, so a second, coloured copy adds no information. Its advantage is coverage: C3-MDIR fills the poles and the left-look gaps from other cycles.
entries.revisitWhen: A published calibration that gives the colour ramp a physical meaning, or a need for gap-free global radar coverage that the FMAP right-look or stereo mosaics cannot supply.

entries.subject: Magellan radio-science free-air gravity, its error, Bouguer anomaly and geoid
entries.finding: PDS Geosciences volume MGN-V-RSS-5-GRAVITY-L2-V1.0 (mg_5201) archives gridded maps only for the degree-120 model SHGJ120P (MGNP120PSAAP, Konopliv and Sjogren 1996): freeair.dat (DMGJ120P, vertical gravity in mGal with its one-sigma error as band 2), geoid.dat (DMOJ120P, metres, with error) and bouguer.dat (DMBJ120P, mGal), 1 x 1 degree, 180 x 360 big-endian float64 on a 6,051.0 km sphere. The degree-180 model MGNP180U (Konopliv et al. 1999) is archived only as coefficients (shgj180u.a01). NASA Trek's Float32 fairgrd, fairerr, bouggrd and geoidgrd layers are conversions of the archive's 8-bit byte-scaled images (1.91 mGal steps), so the float64 grids are preferred. A synthesis of SHGJ120P degrees 2 to 120 reproduces freeair.dat to 0.0037 mGal RMS and geoid.dat to 0.0031 m with longitude centres at integer degrees from 120 W, as the PDS3 labels state; the 2023 PDS4 labels place cell edges there instead, which leaves 5.4 mGal RMS. Values: free-air -100.4 to 386.5 mGal (maximum at Atla Regio, 0.5 N 195 E), error 1.76 to 21.72 mGal, geoid -66.1 to 154.5 m, error 0.14 to 2.29 m, Bouguer -975.8 to 198.1 mGal; the archive catalogue gives free-air errors of about 2 to 12 mGal within 30 degrees of the equator and 15 to 21 at high latitude, and geoid errors of 0.1 to 2.3 m. The shared pds3-grid reader now decodes these images; the gravity, gravity-uncertainty, bouguer and geoid lenses read them unchanged. MGNP180U stays unshown until a coefficient synthesis is added.
